articles.title: Why Token Research Still Matters in DeFi
articles.excerpt: Decentralized finance gives users access to a wide range of digital assets, but accessibility should not replace research. A token being available on a blockchain does not automatically make it trustw…
articles.body: Decentralized finance gives users access to a wide range of digital assets, but accessibility should not replace research. A token being available on a blockchain does not automatically make it trustworthy or suitable for every user. Look Beyond the Token Name Before interacting with an unfamiliar asset, users should verify its contract address, blockchain network, liquidity conditions, and available project documentation. Token names and symbols can be copied, so relying on appearance alone can be risky. It is also worth considering whether the token has enough liquidity for the intended transaction and whether its price may be highly volatile. When using a swap platform such as AviorSwap, these checks remain an important part of responsible decision-making.

articles.title: Why devs should design for blockchain errors, not around them
articles.excerpt: Most of us spend ages polishing the perfect user journey. But in blockchain apps, transactions go sideways more often than we'd like. A wallet rejects the request. The network gets clogged. A tx sits…
articles.body: Most of us spend ages polishing the perfect user journey. But in blockchain apps, transactions go sideways more often than we'd like. A wallet rejects the request. The network gets clogged. A tx sits on "pending" way longer than anyone expected. None of this is rare enough to just shrug off. Errors are part of the experience A generic "Transaction failed" message leaves people with more questions than they started with. Did it get rejected? Did I still pay gas? Should I hit retry, or will that make it worse? Crypto apps need error messages that say what actually happened and what's safe to do next. For swap platforms like AviorSwap, that applies to the whole flow, start to finish. Clear feedback means less confusion and fewer people spamming the same transaction over and over.

articles.title: Two Ethereum Scam Schemes Exposed
articles.excerpt: Two Ethereum Scam Schemes Exposed I build DexMarketCap, a DEX analytics tool with a wallet tracker. The part that matters for this story is how the PnL works: instead of computing a wallet's profit wh…
articles.body: Two Ethereum Scam Schemes Exposed I build DexMarketCap , a DEX analytics tool with a wallet tracker. The part that matters for this story is how the PnL works: instead of computing a wallet's profit when someone opens it, we keep the realized and unrealized PnL of every wallet and every token pre-aggregated in the database, updated live with each swap. That is what makes a wallet page load instantly. It also had a side effect I did not plan for: it gave us a view over every wallet trading on Uniswap at once. So we sorted by success rate. A few wallets had a near-perfect record, hundreds of tokens, hundreds of wins, zero losses. Nobody trades like that.

articles.title: My PDF-to-Markdown converter learned that 'page 3' is a suggestion, and tables are a war crime
articles.excerpt: Spent the last week feeding my PDF-to-Markdown converter a corpus of real-world contracts, annual reports, and academic papers. The lesson: PDF has no concept of 'reading order.' What looks like a cle…
articles.body: Spent the last week feeding my PDF-to-Markdown converter a corpus of real-world contracts, annual reports, and academic papers. The lesson: PDF has no concept of 'reading order.' What looks like a clean two-column layout to your eyes is just a stream of positioned text boxes to the parser. My first naive pass read left-column-top, right-column-top, left-column-bottom — interleaving two unrelated paragraphs into a sentence that made no sense. The fix was a geometric sort: cluster text runs into lines by Y-coordinate, then order lines top-to-bottom, and only apply column detection when a clear vertical gutter exists. Even then, multi-column academic papers with figure captions floating in the margin still bleed into the wrong column.

articles.title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks
articles.excerpt: The fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was one giant gimmick: shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.
articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

articles.title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent 27 more of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23), in its first Starlink launch in 11 days.
articles.body: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Oct. 23, 2026.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission
articles.excerpt: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station . The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts. Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station , they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node. After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module.
